clues: This town is a spa town and borough by a range of soft hills, in the west of its land. It sits just north-east of a great church town.
This town once held the heat crown of its whole land for more than a ten-year span. Rain falls on some one hundred forty days of its year.
This town rose as a spa when spring waters were found here in 1716. Folk came to take the waters, and the town grew from them.
Folk call this the most whole town of the Regency age in its whole land. Its streets still wear that age's face in full.
In March each year, the Gold Cup runs here, the main race of this town's famed meet. Crowds pour in from all the land.
